chapter_theme: Sloth is not a private weakness but the ruin of a lineage: it puts out the family's light, hands a person to enemies, and can be reversed only by the one who harbours it.
structure_note: Parimelazhagar divides the chapter around the evil of sloth (601-604), the qualities that accompany it and their costs (605-608), and the rewards of being free of it (609-610).

601.reading: The unfailing lamp called lineage goes dark and dies when the grime called sloth creeps over it.
601.nuance: A lamp said to be unfailing fails. Parimelazhagar explains மாசு through tamas (தாமத குணம்); that is his Samkhya vocabulary, which the verse does not use.

602.reading: Those who want their family to be a family should conduct themselves with sloth treated as sloth.
602.nuance: The repetition is the verse's device: மடியை மடியா and குடியைக் குடியாக. To be a family is an achievement here, not a birth fact.

positions.position: மடியா means 'as sloth': regard it for what it is, as one says to treat fire as fire. He records the other reading.
positions.quote: நெருப்பிற் கொடியது பிறிதின்மை பற்றி, நெருப்பை நெருப்பாகவே கருதுக

positions.position: மடியா means killing: destroy the habit of sloth.

603.reading: The family of a fool who carries deadly sloth inside him dies before he does.
603.nuance: The cruelty is in the order: he survives to see it. Parimelazhagar's reason is that the family depends on him for support.

604.reading: For those sunk in sloth without any excellent effort, the family declines and faults multiply.
604.nuance: The contrast is not sloth against mere activity but against மாண்ட உஞற்று, refined exertion. The verse thus sets a higher bar than being busy; 607 repeats the phrase.

605.reading: Delay, forgetting, sloth and sleep, these four, are the pleasure-craft of those bound for ruin.
605.nuance: The image lies in காமக் கலன்: a boat you board because you want to, and which then drops you mid-sea. Parimelazhagar records but does not accept a reading of கலன் as a desired ornament. Manakkudavar reads the four as one sequence: delaying a task, forgetting it, slacking, and sleeping instead.

606.reading: Even when what world-rulers possess comes to them, the slothful rarely reach any great fruit.

positions.position: The wealth of world-rulers comes to them unearned, but without effort to guard it, it perishes. He records another reading, that such kings become their allies.
positions.quote: நிலம் முழுவதும் ஆண்டாரது செல்வம் தானே வந்து எய்திய இடத்தும்

positions.position: It is the kings of the earth themselves who, however well provided, lose out if they are slothful.
positions.quote: பூமியையுடைய வேந்தர் பல்பொருளினாலும் அமைந்த விடத் தும் மடியுடையாராயின்

positions.position: படி means worthiness: even those who hold the affection of worthy people get nothing.

607.reading: Those who cling to sloth and make no excellent effort end up hearing words of rebuke and scorn.
607.nuance: கேட்பர் may hold the sting: they can only listen. Parimelazhagar builds a small story from இடி: friends scold first, see no result, and only then turn to contempt, and if friends do this, others need not be mentioned.

608.reading: If sloth settles in one of a family-building nature, it delivers him into slavery to his enemies.
608.nuance: மடிமை, குடிமை and அடிமை rhyme in sequence, and the sound performs the fall from sloth through standing to bondage.

609.reading: When a person ends the rule of sloth over him, the faults that have come into his family and his manhood are gone.
609.nuance: Sloth is a ruler here (மடியாண்மை), and one's own effort deposes it. This is the chapter's one verse of repair. Parimelazhagar makes the promise wide, since even faults from other causes vanish; Manakkudavar limits the faults to neglecting what the family needs.

610.reading: A ruler free from sloth obtains, all at once, the whole expanse crossed by the one who measured with his foot.

positions.position: The one who measured is the deity who spanned all worlds with his stride, and the verse leaves him unnamed.
positions.quote: தன் அடியளவானே எல்லா உலகையும் அளந்த இறைவன்

positions.position: It is a tireless human king who brings every place he goes within his footstep's range.
positions.quote: சோர்வில்லாத ஒரு மன்னன், அவன் சென்ற இடமனைத்தையும்

links.note: 371 says sloth (மடி) arises from a fate of loss. This chapter treats the same மடி as a thing one can depose at will. The tension is direct, and neither chapter acknowledges the other.

The same goal, raising one's family, and the same word used differently. 602 asks one to drive out மடி, and in 1023 the deity tightens its மடி (waist-cloth) and comes ahead of the one who resolves on this. That verse's தான்முந்துறும் also echoes fate's in 380.

Both invoke Vishnu's realm as the highest measure. 610 offers it to the sleepless ruler, and 605 has just listed sleep as a boat to ruin. 1103 asks whether that realm is even as sweet as sleep on a beloved's arms. The Porul and Kamam books rank sleep and sovereignty oppositely.

784 says friendship exists to rebuke when one strays, and uses the same word இடி. If Parimelazhagar is right that the scolding in 607 comes from friends, the verse shows what happens when that duty is carried out and fails.

source_issues: 607: Parimelazhagar's lemma reads மடிந்து புரிந்து where the verse has மடிபுரிந்து.
608: Manakkudavar's commentary is marked as not aligned in the source.
